newsitem.title: INDIA: India truck strike helps firm up edible oil prices.
newsitem.headline: India truck strike helps firm up edible oil prices.

text.p: Indian domestic edible oil prices have risen between 200 rupees and 500 rupees per tonne during the past week as crop arrivals ground to a halt due to a strike by truck owners, industry officials said on Wednesday.
They said existing stocks had been depleted and prices would shoot up if the strike was not averted in another two days.

"Prices have gone up, but so far the strike has not affected the edible oil market very badly due to the stock levels," Navinbhai Shah, president of the Bombay Oilseeds and Oil Exchange Ltd, told Reuters.
"But stocks are fast depleting and the market wants the strike to be ended quickly," Shah said.

An indefinite strike by at least 2.2 million truck owners entered its ninth day on Wednesday. They are protesting a proposed five percent service tax on road transport and a sharp rise in insurance premiums.

Traders said groundnut oil prices had risen to 36,000 rupees per tonne from 35,500 rupees last week and soy oil gained 200 rupees to 28,200 rupees from 28,000 rupees. Palm olein remained steady at 28,500 rupees.
Shah said a ship carrying about 2,000 tonnes of palm olein oil from Malaysia had arrived at the Bombay port but the consignment had not moved out of the port due to the strike.
"Even sunflower oil imports are not coming because news of the strike has reached the other side (Argentina and the United States)," Shah said.
